text:
Alex Wong: heads-up — opened docs PR #234 to clarify caching semantics for `cache_key` and model fallbacks. Preview CI is failing on one snippet, and I need a quick runtime confirmation before I update the text. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/234 :wave:

Anya Petrova: can you paste the current wording? i want to make sure we cover TTL and whether users should include model id in their cache_key.

Alex Wong: current draft says: `If you provide cache_key, we use it to cache prefix outputs.` that's too vague. also example shows `cache_key: user-123` but doesn't explain collision scope.

Ryan K.: quick answer from runtime: the runtime composes the effective cache namespace as `<model_id>|<route_id>|<user_cache_key>` when user supplies `cache_key`. by default there is no need to include model id in the user `cache_key` — we already scope it.

Anya Petrova: perfect — do we invalidate on model variant fallback? e.g., if routing falls back to `gptx-quant` from `gptx` is the cache reused? that's an edge case we need spelled out.

Ryan K.: good catch. behavior: if the fallback is to a model variant with a different `model_id` string, the composed namespace changes (because `<model_id>` changes) so the cache is NOT reused. That avoids serving KV blobs incompatible with different tokenization/quantization.

Maria S.: that's the behavior we want documented. also what's the default TTL? the examples should show a number.

Ryan K.: default TTL is `3600` (seconds) for prefix caches. we expose `cache_ttl_seconds` in config. note: customers can set `0` for no expiry but we discourage it for unbounded memory growth.

Anya Petrova: can you confirm format for examples? i'd like a minimal YAML snippet to copy into the PR.

Ryan K.: snippet you can use:

```yaml
cache:
  cache_key: "user-123"   # appended to model+route to form namespace
  cache_ttl_seconds: 3600  # default TTL (1 hour)
```

Alex Wong: thanks — i'll paste that into the PR. one more question: what about multi-tenant shared routes? Will `route_id` be the same across tenants?

Ryan K.: `route_id` is per-configured route in the customer's deployment. for multi-tenant setups it's typically the route name (so collisions can happen if multiple tenants share a route). recommend docs call out: for tenant isolation, include a tenant identifier in `cache_key` (or use dedicated route per tenant).

Anya Petrova: ok i'll add a short note: `For multi-tenant routes, include tenant id in cache_key to avoid cross-tenant collisions.`

Alex Wong: docs-ci-bot the preview is failing right now with lint error re: code fence language — i think the preview build logs show it. @docs-ci-bot can you re-run after i update?

Alex Wong: fixed — added `yaml` to fence and updated wording per Ryan. pushed new commit.

Maria S.: i can do a quick review for wording and examples. assigning myself as reviewer.

Anya Petrova: i'll do technical review once maria is done.

Maria S.: reviewed, small nit about phrasing around `0` TTL (suggest "not recommended"). left inline comment.

Alex Wong: addressed nit, pushed. can i merge after 1 more approval? we need this in the 1.12 docs ship today.

Anya Petrova: approving now — LGTM from runtime side. :thumbsup:

Alex Wong: merging now. thanks all! :shipit:
